messages:
maya: Customer (QuoteGen) opened an escalation — after today's rollout their contract-summarizer output lost bullet separation and started inserting 'Ref:' lines in the middle of sections. They say it worked yesterday.

maya: Paste from customer: 
```
Prompt template v1: 'Summarize contract: {{clauses}} -- bullets only'
Prompt sent today with an extra trailing space after the variable: 'Summarize contract: {{clauses}}  -- bullets only'
```

maya: They included API request/response snippet. Response used model 'redwood-compact-v2' and returned a fused paragraph and stray 'Ref:' tokens. Also no hashed line items. Customer says this broke their downstream parsing.

devon: @maya can you paste the minimal request (headers + body) and the model hash? any quantization changes in the rollout? :thinking:

maya: Request body snippet they sent: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{
  "model": "redwood-compact-v2",
  "input": "Summarize contract: {{clauses}}  -- bullets only",
  "max_tokens": 320,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

maya: They emphasized the only change was one extra space after the placeholder. They can reproduce reliably.

devon: Hmm — we pushed a canary earlier with a kernel selection tweak and prefix cache deduping. Deploy log: canary-id=2026-03-12-rc4, image=runtime:v3.2.0-qopt. @sam any known tokenization delta?

sam: deploy-bot: Deployed canary 2026-03-12-rc4 to us-west1 (20% traffic).

sam: I saw the canary notes: switched tokenizer fallback when encountering double spaces near braces to use byte-level fallback for speed on compact models. That could change how {{clauses}} + trailing space tokenizes.

devon: If trailing space changes token boundaries, model may lose the explicit list markers we rely on. Could be a tokenization -> decoding/regression combo. Need repro with raw token ids. @maya can customer send the encoded tokens or allow us to re-run with their input?

maya: Customer ok to share examples. Pasted the token ids they observed for the two variants. (shortened)
```
with single space tokens: [120, 87, 541, ... , 14]
with double space tokens: [120, 87, 541, 0, 14]
```

maya: They also attached generated text: one variant preserves bullet markers ('- Clause A\n- Clause B') the other produces 'Clause A Ref: Clause B' fused.

devon: That matches a decode boundary issue. Two options: 1) rollback tok fallback in canary, 2) patch decoding to respect placeholder tokenization for templated inputs. Which do we prefer short-term?

elaine: Product note: this affects several customers using template-based extractors. Rolling back canary would be fastest minimize impact. We should also add a mitigation: detect templates with braces and force model variant that uses full-tokenizer for now.

sam: I'll scale canary back to 0% in us-west1 and trigger a quick A/B rerun on the failing examples. Doing now. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary 2026-03-12-rc4 scaled to 0% in us-west1 by sam at 1902101299.

sam: Re-ran the customer's examples on stable runtime and canary binary with logging. Stable output matches pre-rollout expected bullets. Canary reproduces fused 'Ref:' token. Raw logs attached to ticket 4521.

devon: Good repro. Let's mark P0 for rollback confirmed. I'll draft a root-cause note: tokenizer fallback + placeholder trailing whitespace -> token alignment shift -> decoder produces token sequence that inserts 'Ref:' string due to model learned pattern.

maya: Customer updated ticket saying rollback resolved their issue for now and asked for timeline to prevent recurrence.

elaine: Action items:
- sam: revert tokenizer fallback in next patch (PR #7890).
- devon: add unit tests for templated placeholders with variable whitespace and verify token ids stable.
- maya: send customer ETA and offer temporary dedicated route to stable models if they want.

maya: Customer thanked us and will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll keep the logs and repro attached to internal issue. Moving to tracking board.

devon: Also add a quick eval: run our prompt-sensitivity harness across top 50 templated customers to catch similar regressions before rollouts.

elaine: Agreed. Let's meet 30m to prioritize mitigations.

maya: Thanks all — closing the slack escalation for now, follow-ups in ticket 4521 and PR #7890.
